questions.q: What term describes a chemical reaction or process that releases thermal energy into the surroundings, causing the temperature to rise?
What term describes a chemical reaction or process that absorbs thermal energy from its surroundings, causing the temperature to drop?
Which of the following everyday events is a classic example of an exothermic chemical reaction?
What happens to the temperature of the surroundings during an exothermic reaction?
What happens to the temperature of the surroundings during an endothermic process?
a: It decreases as heat is absorbed from the environment

questions.q: Which of the following processes is strictly endothermic?
a: Thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate by heating

questions.q: When solid ammonium nitrate dissolves in water and the temperature of the water drops significantly, what type of process is this?
Why does the temperature of a reaction mixture rise when an acid reacts with a reactive metal or alkali?
a: It is an exothermic reaction releasing thermal energy

questions.q: Which of the following is a reliable way to test if a chemical reaction in a test tube is exothermic?
a: Feel the outside of the test tube to see if it feels warm or hot
Weigh the test tube on a balance
Listen for a loud humming sound

questions.q: In terms of energy, how can combustion (burning) reactions be classified?
a: Endothermic because they need heat to start
Exothermic because they release large amounts of heat and light energy

questions.q: Which of the following phase changes from a higher energy state to a lower energy state is exothermic?
Which phase change requires an input of thermal energy from the surroundings and is therefore endothermic?
During a laboratory neutralization reaction between hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide solution, a thermometer placed in the beaker shows an increase in temperature. What does this indicate?
Why is photosynthesis in green plants classified as an endothermic process?
a: It gives off heat to the room
It absorbs light energy from the Sun to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose
It releases oxygen gas with high heat

questions.q: If you mix two chemicals in a beaker and notice frost forming on the outside because the temperature drops below freezing, what type of reaction has occurred?
Which statement correctly describes energy changes during bond breaking and bond forming?
a: Breaking bonds releases energy while forming bonds absorbs energy
Both breaking and forming bonds absorb energy
Both breaking and forming bonds release energy
Breaking bonds absorbs energy while forming bonds releases energy

questions.q: What type of energy is primarily transferred to the surroundings during an exothermic chemical reaction?
What happens to chemical energy stored within bonds when an exothermic reaction takes place?
a: It is converted and released as thermal or light energy into the surroundings
It remains trapped inside the atoms permanently
It turns into electricity directly without wires

questions.q: Which of the following reactions is typically used in commercial instant cold packs for sports injuries?
a: Dissolving specific salts like ammonium nitrate in water (endothermic)
Mixing water and concentrated sulfuric acid

questions.q: Which of the following reactions is typically used in commercial instant heat packs for warming hands?
a: Exothermic oxidation of iron powder with oxygen

questions.q: When wood burns in a fireplace, thermal and light energy are given off. How is this classified?
If a chemical reaction absorbs more energy when breaking bonds than it releases when making new bonds, what is the overall reaction?
What change would you expect to observe on a thermometer when an endothermic reaction takes place in solution?
Which of the following processes involves both absorbing energy to break bonds and releasing energy to form new bonds?
Which of the following best defines an exothermic process?
a: A process where energy is transferred from the system to the surroundings
A process where energy is transferred from surroundings to system
A process with zero energy transfer
A process that only occurs in a vacuum

questions.q: Which of the following best defines an endothermic process?
a: A process where energy is absorbed by the system from the surroundings
A process that creates thermal energy

questions.q: During the thermal decomposition of copper(II) carbonate in a test tube, continuous heating is required. What does this tell us about the reaction?
a: It releases large amounts of light

questions.q: When concentrated sulfuric acid is added to water, the solution becomes extremely hot. How is this dissolution process classified?
If the products of a reaction have less chemical potential energy stored in their bonds than the reactants, where did the excess energy go?
a: Released into the surroundings as heat or light

questions.q: If the products of a reaction have more chemical potential energy stored in their bonds than the reactants, what must have happened during the reaction?
a: Energy was absorbed from the surroundings

questions.q: Which of the following everyday appliances relies on an exothermic reaction to function?
Why does food cook when placed in a hot oven?
a: The food releases heat into the oven
The food creates its own nuclear energy
Thermal energy is transferred endothermically into the food molecules

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true regarding respiration in living cells?
a: It is an exothermic process that releases energy for body functions
It is an endothermic process that absorbs heat from blood

questions.q: What role do surroundings play in an exothermic reaction?
a: They provide heat to the reaction
They absorb the thermal energy released by the reaction
They remain completely isolated and unaffected
They act as a chemical catalyst

questions.q: What role do surroundings play in an endothermic reaction?
a: They supply thermal energy to the reacting system

questions.q: Which of the following laboratory observations confirms that a chemical change is exothermic?
a: The flask gets cold to the touch
The temperature of the reaction mixture increases noticeably

questions.q: When a candle burns, wax reacts with oxygen in the air. What energy transformation takes place?
a: Chemical energy is transformed into thermal and light energy (exothermic)
Thermal energy is absorbed from the air

questions.q: Is the boiling of water an exothermic or endothermic process?
a: Endothermic because water must absorb heat continuously to change into gas

questions.q: Which term describes the minimum amount of energy required to start a chemical reaction?
What happens when you mix baking soda and vinegar in a flask and observe a temperature decrease?
a: An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the liquid and container
